_comment: folio-assist-core — THE CONTENT LAYER, in folio-assistant-core/ per the owner (2026-09-20: "use folio-assistant-core/") — the DIRECTORY and the declared NAME are BOTH spelled out in full. They were briefly different -- directory `folio-assistant-core`, name `folio-assist-core` -- and this comment went on asserting the short name after the `name` field beside it had already been changed, so the file contradicted itself in adjacent lines. Corrected 2026-09-20. WHAT IS STILL SHORT, DELIBERATELY, IS THE LANDING CARD ID below: a card id is a PUBLISHED IDENTIFIER and does not move with a directory. `landing-sticky.test.ts` says so and bean `8xtj` records the cost of assuming the two are one string -- a session sweeping every spelling at once renamed the card by accident and had to put it back. Main created a folio-assistant-core/ stub the same day; the two were one instance under two paths, and instanceRoots is keyed on the declared name, so the stub and the populated one collided on one key and the stub won. Consolidated here, declared as a real instance on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20 ("Create f-a-core/ as a real instance now"). It declared NO directories when it was created, deliberately, because the modules it would own were still interleaved under cat-harness/ and declaring a directory that is not there is the dh4f defect. They are NOT interleaved any more: bean frs5's branch wrote `schemas/` (dublin-core, catalogue, materialization, library-ref) and `folios/`, and they moved in here rather than staying under a SECOND directory declaring this same name. Two instances with one declared name is not a layout question: `instanceRoots` is keyed on the declared name, so the stub and the populated one were one key and the stub won. The original note read: the modules it will own are still interleaved with the harness's under cat-harness/, and declaring a directory that is not there is the dh4f defect — every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. An instance that declares only what it has is honest; one that declares its target layout is a lie a gate cannot catch. scripts/repo-partition.ts is the machine-readable statement of what will move here.

stickies.body:
The knowledge graph is four sub-graphs, and an instance declares which of them it holds.

**Content** is what somebody authors and a reader reads — this layer's subject. **Skills** are the instructions an agent follows to do the work. **Processes** are the BPMN diagrams that say who does what, in which order, and where the gates are — they are executable, not illustrations. **Tools** are what an agent can call.

Getting anything in is **acquisition**: unstructured and semi-structured sources arrive through `uploads/` or through the conversation, and are ingested into `library/`. It is a step rather than a graph kind of its own — there is no fifth directory to look for.

**Scope:** the content model — what a folio IS. Not the skills and tools that operate on it, and not any particular folio's chapters.

directories.description: The content layer's own schema nodes. Three today, and they are one chain: `dublin-core` is what a source system SAYS about an item, `catalogue` is the shape of the collection that item sits in, and `materialization` is whether any of its bytes are actually here. The third is the load-bearing one — see its module doc for why bootstrap fetching a harness and who-iris fetching three items out of 361.55 GB are the same process with two names.

What an AUTHOR creates using the graph -- a note, a visualization, a paper. Owner, 2026-09-20: 'folios/ would be a note, visualization, paper etc that user/author is creating referencing the KG... folios in f-a-core as it is about KG management workflows built on cat-harness document rendering justthedocs simple rendering.' It declares the EXISTING `folio` kind rather than a new one: `folio` is already 'authored content, rendered to a website', registered by core because only core can render it, and a second kind for the same thing would be two spellings of one concept. The contrast is with `docs` in cat-harness, whose subject is the harness itself. Worked example of the distinction: the who-iris catalogue goes in `library/` or is referenced remotely; a note ABOUT it is a folio; the page explaining how ingestion works is docs.

Core's glossary (owner, 2026-09-23: "put glossary into folio-assistant-core", "part of general pracice w/ glossary/ page"): folio-glossary/v1 documents, each a SKOS concept scheme of local terms linked to external SKOS concepts by exactMatch/closeMatch, plus external concepts listed as members without being copied. A whole external scheme is referenced through remoteGraphs with graphKinds ["glossary"]. `dependents: reproduce` so every folio built on core gets its own glossary/, which is what makes a glossary general practice rather than a harness feature. Rendered on the glossary/ page with the swimlane ledger (cat-harness's `swimlane-glossary`) as one more source; checked by `check:glossary`.

Voice skills this layer owns. `technical-writer` is the whole of it: an SDO register (W3C, IHE) with RFC 2119 requirement levels, read from the two ingested RFCs and constrained by RFC 8174. PLACED HERE BY JUDGEMENT, on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-21: *"voices should be associated to appropriate home semantically/by judgement"*. It arrived on `main` in `cat-harness/voices/` while the migration to `<instance>/skills/voices/` was in flight (bean `btuv`), and the two obvious mechanical homes are both wrong — the PLATFORM holds no voice content, and `agent-skills` merely holds the RFCs it cites, which has never decided ownership (`who-editorial` cites who-iris's library and lives in who-style-guide). What settles it is what the voice is ABOUT: how to write technical documentation of a standard, software or a knowledge asset — which is what this layer is for.

The content layer's Tool nodes. Declared 2026-09-22 with the first one, `folio-changeset` (bean jwox, epic q4jm), which exposes `schemas/changeset.ts`. Reached by the harness through tool auto-discovery (bean p0za, owner ruling 2026-09-22), never by an import: the harness may not import core, and a Tool node is a declaration loaded by path.

The review-comment Tool and its move helper, with their tests beside them. Core declared its `schemas/`, its `folios/`, its `voices/` and its `tools/` and left `scripts/` undeclared, which is the `ylj7` shape: the directories that hold what is DESCRIBED were declared and the one holding what RUNS was not. Declared where it is: `review-comments.ts` is invoked by path from `folio-staging.yml`, so relocating it is an invocation surface `check:workflow-paths` would have to re-guard for nothing the declaration does not already buy.
